subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` self-pause tool, and if so should it be implemented as a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted tool with explicit sandbox and cap policy?
rationale: The request changes core model-facing tools and gateway/session scheduling semantics, and automation cannot safely choose the long-term API, configuration, interruption, restart, or sandbox contract.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or replacement to prove same-session resume, interruption cancellation, cap enforcement, restart behavior, and sandbox policy.

options.title: Keep existing scheduling surfaces
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and document cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` as the supported patterns.

options.title: Narrow to extension API work
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension seam if maintainers want optional sleep behavior outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or replacement to prove same-session resume, interruption cancellation, cap enforcement, restart behavior, and sandbox policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime, gateway, cron-adjacent, and product-surface history makes this the strongest available owner for the API and security choice.
